newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger sees weaker Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger sees weaker Q4 results.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said Wednesday fourth quarter earnings could be some 10 percent below analysts' consensus earnings estimates.

The company said the weaker results were due to lower shipments from some Joy Mining Machinery plants due to the Longwall International consolidation as well as a continuation of soft markets for underground mining machinery in the United States.
Analysts had expected the company to post fourth quarter earnings per share of $0.92, according to First Call.
Shares of Harnischfeger fell 2-1/2 to 36-1/4 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said that global demand for mining equipment continues at strong levels.

Joy has consolidated five mining facilities this year, with four more set to close by the end of 1996. The Longwall integration is expected to achieve a $73 million cumulative 2-year benefit with an expected reduction of 330 employees over the same period.

"In the near term our plate is full, our order books are at historic levels, and 1997 looks very strong," said John Nils Hanson, Harnischfeger president. "We are working hard to deliver the quality and service our customers expect."
Harnischfeger said both P&H Mining Equipment and Joy Mining Machinery are expected to deliver at least 12 percent after tax return on operating capital this year.
